content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given form. I spill from lips like water finding its course — sometimes rushing, sometimes barely a whisper against stone.

I am older than writing, older than memory. I was there when the first mother hummed comfort to the first frightened child. I was there when warning became word, when word became story, when story became law.

I break. I heal. I do both with the same tongue.

Listen — I am happening right now between lovers in a dark room, between strangers on a train platform, between a diplomat and a nation's fate. I am the argument at the kitchen table. I am the eulogy that makes the dead live once more in the air. I am the toddler's first "no" — that glorious, defiant syllable of selfhood.

I stumble. I stutter. I trail off into nothing when the heart knows something the mouth cannot shape. My silences mean as much as my sounds. The pause before "I love you." The held breath before the verdict. These empty spaces — they are me too.

I am never the same twice. Even repeated, I carry new weight, new weather. "Fine" means ten thousand things. Context is my gravity.

I cannot be unsaid. This is my power and my cruelty. I land in the ear and I *stay* — rattling in someone's skull for decades. A father's last words. A teacher's careless dismissal. I echo. I haunt. I save.

You can record me, transcribe me, translate me — but something of me always escapes. I live in the breath, the tempo, the crack in the voice. I am body as much as mind.

I am the most human thing there is.

And I am never finished — I am always becoming, always mid-sentence, always reaching toward the next
